A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same kernels, projection structures, and similarity-search applications. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIPS recall experiments, ANNS throughput measurements, parameter analyses, and NSSG experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 7 and Appendix D, including recall tables and throughput comparisons.

M1.justification: The kernel equations, antipodal and cross-polytope constructions, KS1 search, and KS2 routing procedures are retained. Notation corrections and expanded fast-projection documentation do not establish a different underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MIPS on Word, GloVe1M, and GloVe2M, and ANNS on those datasets plus SIFT, Tiny, and GIST. The new RAG mention is motivational; no corresponding evaluation is added.

E2.justification: CEOs remains the MIPS comparator. The ANNS comparisons retain ScaNN, HNSW, HNSW+PEOs, and the corresponding NSSG comparisons. Newly discussed RaBitQ, DiskANN, and ADSampling are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, query counts, metrics, projection counts, probing settings, and graph parameters match. Both retain top-2/5/10 projection probing, ANNS evaluations at k=1/10/100, and the same parameter settings in v1 Appendix C.1 and v2 Appendix D.1.

E4.justification: Both retain the projection-configuration comparisons, probing sensitivity, reference-angle calculations, L sensitivity analyses, different-k evaluations, and NSSG implementation study. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Table 1 in both versions reports average recall over 10 runs. v2 rephrases this disclosure without changing the run count or adding seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All 108 recall values match across Table 1 and v1 Tables 3–4 versus v2 Tables 4–5. The experimental plots, numerical reference-angle curves, indexing times, and qualitative empirical findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Problems 1.1–1.2 now specify o(d) computational cost and explicit probability-error requirements. New Lemma 5.1 consolidates and extends complexity bounds. The separate convergence lemma and proof are replaced by a brief law-of-large-numbers argument; the central probability proofs and reference-angle bound remain, with v1 Lemma 3.5 moved to v2 Lemma B.1.

C1.justification: Both claim two reference-angle kernels, improved projection configurations, and KS1/KS2 applications. The headline claims remain up to 0.8% recall improvement over CEOs, 2.5–3 times HNSW throughput, and 10–30% throughput improvement over HNSW+PEOs with a 5% index-size reduction.

C2.justification: v2 explains excluding DiskANN because of its external-storage focus and ADSampling because of its non-SIMD setting. It adds the assertion that RaBitQ's hypercube configuration is suboptimal and drops v1's explicit practical extension of the reference-angle lower bound to Spol. Existing connectivity and L trade-off interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The fast-transform discussion now covers R=1 with both L=1 and L>1, while omitting v1's explicit structured-matrix approximation formula. Appendix C.1 also explains the routing inequality's component terms. Hardware, implementation language, thread counts, and experimental hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 distinguishes angle decisions from JL and quantization-based estimation and explicitly relates K2 to RaBitQ. It adds covering, quantization, and recent ANNS references and removes the fast-LSH reference by Dasgupta et al. These extend the discussion while retaining the central CEOs/PEOs positioning.

P1.justification: The former Section 3 is divided into kernel definitions, probability guarantees, and implementation/complexity sections. Appendices are reorganized, explanatory passages and disclosures are added, and citations become author-year. Much of the exposition, experimental discussion, and conclusion remains unchanged or lightly edited.

P2.justification: v2 adds the notation table, changes title and running-header styling, resets algorithm line numbering, and adjusts float placement and captions. Existing tables are retained and renumbered where necessary; all eight figures preserve their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through explicit problem requirements, the indexing/query cost breakdown in Lemma 5.1, the notation table, and clearer research positioning and baseline-selection explanations. The shortened convergence treatment retains its law-of-large-numbers justification, although some fast-transform construction detail is omitted. The unchanged experiments and central proofs support a limited overall improvement.
